newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND BANK AIMS TO KEEP MARKKA NEAR CENTRAL RATE.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND BANK AIMS TO KEEP MARKKA NEAR CENTRAL RATE.

text.p: Bank of Finland board of management member Matti Vanhala on Monday repeated that the Bank's policy is to try to keep the markka close to its ERM central parity rate of 3.04 per German mark.

"Our ambition is to keep the exchange rate close to the central rate in order to have as stable (exchange) rates as possible," Vanhala told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) in an interview due to be broadcast later this week.
"To the extent you can analyse these things ... all calculations tend to confirm that the (DEM/FIM) central rate should be around three (markka per mark)," he said.

When asked whether the central bank was worried about a potential new wave of speculative interests in the markka like earlier in the year when the Finnish unit briefly gained sharply against the mark, Vanhala said:
"We have assumed all along that life in the ERM means that at times there will be strong waves of appreciation or in the other direction."
The markka was linked to ERM in October last year.
